h: Getting the most from a Granite City science day
p: Science centres reward a bit of strategy. Head for whichever zone your lot are most excited about first, while energy levels are sky high, and save the calmer corners for later when legs start to flag. If there's a live show or demonstration on the day, build your visit around it rather than stumbling across it halfway through, because they're often the bit kids talk about all the way home.

Most families find a couple of hours is about right, maybe a little longer with very curious children. That leaves plenty of the day for the rest of the city, and Constitution Street is handily placed for it. Head down towards the sea and you'll find Footdee, or Fittie as locals call it, a tiny old fishing village of cottages and quirky sheds tucked at the harbour end of the beach. It's one of the most charming little corners of Aberdeen and great for a wander.

If the science bug has properly bitten, Aberdeen Maritime Museum on Shiprow tells the story of the city's relationship with the sea, from shipbuilding and fishing to the North Sea oil and gas industry. That pairs nicely with all the energy talk inside the science centre.
Granite looks its best in the sunshine, so if the weather turns kind, take a stroll along Union Street and look up at the buildings. On a wild day, though, you've already picked the right place.
